newsitem.title: CANADA: CanOxy boosts Yemen Masila oil reserves.
newsitem.headline: CanOxy boosts Yemen Masila oil reserves.

text.p: Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd said on Friday that strong second-quarter drilling performance fueled a 76 million barrel boost of its share of proved reserves on its Masila Block in Yemen.

CanOxy said the development drilling, along with additional seismic information, combined to lift its net proved reserves on the block to 169 million barrels and increase its reserve life to five years.
The company said it identified additional reservoir optimization and exploration opportunities through recent work, which was expected to mean more reserve additions in the next few months.
Three weeks ago, CanOxy said it made a new field discovery on the Masila Block called Dahban, which was awaiting tests.
During the second-quarter, Masila production averaged a record 189,400 barrels a day -- 98,500 net to CanOxy -- and reached a one-day high of 210,000 barrels on June 25, it said.
CanOxy's share of average production during last year's second quarter was 94,700 barrels a day.

"While Masila production has been on an upward trend since commencement of operations in 1993, growth has accelerated in 1997 as a result of development drilling and field extensions," the company said.
CanOxy is operator and owns 52 percent of Masila. Partners include a unit of Royal Dutch/Shell Group, Occidental Petroleum Corp and a Middle East-based construction company.
Company-wide, CanOxy's production averaged 188,000 barrels of crude oil and 422 million cubic feet of natural gas a day in the second quarter.
That was up from 138,000 barrels of oil and 227 million cubic feet of gas a day last year.
Much of the increase came from its North American division after the takeover in the quarter of Wascana Energy Inc.

CanOxy said it exited June pumping out 72,000 barrels of conventional oil and 322 million cubic feet of gas a day in Canada, compared to an average of 61,000 barrels of oil and 290 million cubic feet of gas a day for the quarter.
"Further growth is expected over the balance of the year," the company said. "Rigs and services are under contract and 420 wells are scheduled to be drilled in the third and fourth quarters."
CanOxy earlier reported second-quarter cash flow of C$193 million or C$1.42 a share, up from C$175 million or C$1.29 a share in the same period of 1996.
Earnings were C$20 million or C$0.15 a share, down from C$47 million or C$0.35 a share last year.
The drop in profits reflected higher depletion costs associated with the Wascana merger and an inability to deduct the costs for tax purposes, CanOxy said.
